card: This PR adds a delay_for parameter to sendrawtransaction that delays broadcast over private connections by a specified duration plus randomized jitter. Delayed transactions are queued in memory and re-validated against the mempool by a periodic scheduler task before outbound connections are requested. All rationale comes solely from the PR author, with no linked issue. Pending delayed transactions are not saved to disk and will be lost if the node restarts before release.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete implementation diff: introduces the `ReleaseDelayedPrivateBroadcast` scheduled loop in `PeerManager`, mempool re-validation (`ProcessTransaction` test accept) upon release, delay jitter formulas, and unit/fuzz/functional tests.
evidence: PR description: "Allow a user to submit a transaction for delayed broadcasting, that will be broadcast only later, at a randomized time. The aim is increased privacy, by making time-correlation-based tracking more difficult."
All claims of utility and necessity originate solely from the author.
problem: Broadcasting a transaction immediately allows network adversaries to correlate transaction submission time with user activity or off-chain events. Users wanting to obfuscate submission timing must rely on external cron jobs or custom daemons, which risk revealing node connection timing.

risk.why: Bugs in delay scheduling or re-validation could cause transactions to be silently dropped or fail to broadcast over private connections, while the lack of persistence can lead to forgotten transactions on node restart.

scope_notes: The implementation relies on private broadcast infrastructure (`-privatebroadcast`). Delayed transactions are not persisted to disk and are permanently lost if the node shuts down or crashes before the delay elapses.
summary: Adds an optional `delay_for` parameter to the `sendrawtransaction` RPC to hold back private transaction broadcasts. Delayed transactions are queued in memory, randomized with extra jitter (at least 5 minutes and up to 50% of the requested delay), and scheduled for release by `PeerManager`. Before broadcasting via outbound privacy network connections, due transactions are re-validated against the mempool.
